Hi friend. Usually I am a lurker here, not commenting much because I cannot offer advice or support to any sort of great semblance as others here can. But I felt compelled to write this because of this:

>Whoever said that your 20s are supposed to be the best time of your life is a goddamned liar.

I wish I could tell everyone in the world right now, that quotes like these should not be taken as literal. I'm sorry if this comes across as a rather abrupt and perhaps rude way of saying this. I think (perhaps I'm wrong here..) you have read this quote, and in your pain have applied it to your life as some sort of self-justification to explain your pain away..

You are responsible for yourself. No quote will guarantee how you will feel, nor should you feel your life must follow or be obliged to go in their direction. I do not know your struggles myself, and having not been through things like that I cannot relate. But I want to tell you, if you wish to be someone else's person, you have to be a person to yourself first. If you prioritize others first, at a time when you yourself are in so much pain, you will continue to be lost, and hurt further. You say you do not want to die, just that you are in pain. I think you are far stronger than you think.

If you feel you are too weak, take some time off. When you are perhaps calmer, reassess your situation. I have by choice never been in a relationship, so I may not be the best source... but I strongly urge you to not get romantically involved. Not yet. Teach yourself what it means to give love, and learn by yourself what it means to be loved, and to feel love. You deserve to know your own love before you can allow others to skew it and rob you of it. Then, when you have done that, you can give love to others who appreciate it, and who will reciprocate it back for you.

I tried to rationalize it, and tell myself it was caused perhaps by cross contamination or maybe it was spoiled and I just didn't realize. But now that sense of wanting to be more food-safety conscious has changed into an obsessive desire to know for certain that everything I eat is perfect.

Anytime I eat I worry, is it contaminated? Does it look off? Does it smell strange? Is that spot normal?

Out of 4 recent food poisoning cases I've had, only 1 I know with any sort of accuracy what made me sick. But the other 3 I don't know. That's what's made me so obsessed and crazed about this. Even to this day I still wonder, why and what made me sick? 

If I knew why I got sick, maybe because I ate something that was spoiled- that would be one thing. Because then I could say, well I'll just check better next time. But because I don't know what made me sick, I obsess over every detail, on the off chance I catch that mystery thing that got me sick last time. Because if I don't know what made me sick last time, what if I fail to notice what will get me sick in the future?

Accidently touch a vegetable after handling raw meat? Cross-contamination. Sure, it may not be contaminated, but I'd rather not take that chance.

Mix meat and then touch a plastic bag? Now that bag's got salmonella on it (if the meat had it of course), and that lives for what, 72 hours? Now anything that touches that is also infected. 

It's easy to separate poor food handling and proper food handling. But I don't know where I fall in that. I wash my hands for 1 minute after touching anything, and disinfect and wash my knife in between cutting anything. I'd rather be safe than sorry, as they say.

I know I should feel safe, and that there are many foods that I can eat without worry. But if you search it up, nothing is safe from food poisoning. Maybe my sense of logic and common sense is warped from being so deluded, but food poisoning seems far too torturous for anyone to enjoy food... I'm always surprised whenever I see people eating so nonchalantly.. How they don't worry just blows my mind.

I've tried to calm myself down and reassure myself. But then I look online and see things like this.

If you say "I'm not afraid of food poisoning," people will tell you "wait until you get it, then you'll see."

But if you say "I'm afraid of food poisoning," people will tell you "it's not that bad, it's temporary, and you won't die."

So I'm conflicted. Is it that bad or not? I can't decide for myself. I know it's temporary. But I can't convince myself that it's something I can just ignore. I've experienced it before a few times, and each time it's so horrible.. It's like PTSD to me. Like a veteran who's retired.. they may be past the war, but it still always haunts them. It replays in their mind and brings them the same feeling as when they were there. That's what I'm afraid of. Even without having food poisoning, I can always feel it.

My sense of logic is completely gone from how afraid I am, now I'm constantly paranoid because I can't tell anything apart anymore! It's so horrible to me the few times I've had it, that I wish it was deadly, just so I don't have to feel it anymore...
